stimulus.source_note: Title page of a 1665 German edition of Bartolome de las Casas, public domain (Wikimedia Commons).
stimulus.text: Title page of a 1665 German edition of Bartolome de las Casas's writings about Spanish actions in the Americas. The title page is in German, the book was printed in northern Europe, and the scenes around the title show Spanish soldiers attacking Indigenous people and forcing them to carry goods. Las Casas wrote his account in Spanish in 1542.

stem: The term 'Black Legend' was first used by a Spanish historian in 1914 to describe anti-Spanish propaganda, and students are warned to weigh the authorship and motives of English sources from the 1500s onward. Which of the following best explains why the 1914 origin of the term matters for a student reading a 1500s English account of Spanish cruelty?

options.text: It shows English accounts of Spanish cruelty cannot be trusted at all and must be ignored
options.misconception: Overstates the warning; the books say weigh the motives, not ignore the accounts.

options.text: It shows Spanish cruelty never happened and the English accounts were invented from nothing at all
options.misconception: Confuses propaganda with invention; Spanish cruelty is not in question, only the extent and the motive behind the telling.

options.text: It shows the 1500s accounts were written by Spanish officials, not by Spain's rivals in Europe
options.misconception: Reverses the authorship; the accounts came from Spain's rivals, not from Spanish officials.

options.text: The term is a later label, so each 1500s source must be judged on its own authorship

instruction: Answer from the stimulus and stem only. Pick one option. Do not open the question file.
